name: KY-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent McGarvey running with large cash advantage ($1.8M on hand)
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
No polls or expert ratings available
model.rationale: McGarvey combines incumbency, a heavily Democratic-leaning Louisville seat, and a dominant fundraising edge over an underfunded challenger, while markets price his reelection near 95%. The fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit margin.
model.watch: A late surge of outside Republican spending or an unexpectedly strong national GOP environment could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Morgan McGarvey seeks a second term representing this Louisville-based district, which leans Democratic by about ten points. He enters the general election with roughly $1.8 million on hand after raising over $1.6 million, while Republican challenger Maria Rodriquez reports no significant fundraising. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give McGarvey about a 95 percent chance of winning.

The fundamentals support a comfortable Democratic hold: the district's partisan lean, incumbency advantage, and financial dominance all point the same direction. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which keeps the margin estimate broad, but nothing in the available evidence suggests a competitive race.
